newsitem.title: USA: Rubin offers no advice on single Euroepan currency.
newsitem.headline: Rubin offers no advice on single Euroepan currency.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Monday he does not want to offer Europeans advice on a single currency and that the view from Washington is that what is good for Europe is good for the United States.
"I don't think it is for us to have views," Rubin said when asked what the United States thought of Europe's move to a single currency.

"Europeans are going to have to figure out what is best for Europe," Rubin added. "We have nothing to fear in any of this. In fact if Europe is better off, we're better off, because there are better markets for us."

Rubin said told a meeting of the Bretton Woods/Overseas Development Counci that the European single currency would likely be discussed at the upcoming meeting of leaders of the Group of Seven rich industrial nations.
